speaker_role: current admissions officer (Christine Bowman, senior admissions administrator, demoing her own institution's CRM live)
commercial_incentive: none evident; part of College Essay Guy's educational podcast/interview series
key_insights: Colleges commonly use CRM software (demoed: Slate) that visually timelines every interaction a prospective student has with the institution over years, including opens, clicks, event attendance, and portal logins
Tracked interactions include college fair inquiry cards, email opens/clicks, visit-day and event attendance, completed interviews, and application portal engagement
Admissions staff can drill into a single email to see exactly when, how, and for how long it was opened and on what device
Demonstrated interest is framed as 'meeting in the middle' rather than pure counting up or down; colleges try to reach students through whatever channel they actually use (email, text, etc.)
Simply opening emails, clicking through, and spending time on the website (some schools track dwell time) are low-lift but real, free interest signals
Virtual/remote engagement, which expanded greatly post-pandemic, counts fully as demonstrated interest, especially for students who cannot visit in person
specific_numbers_or_facts: Example applicant record shown spans tracked interactions from 2014 to 2021 (Christine Bowman, using her own child's admissions file as the demo, with permission)
Second example: inquiry card filled out at a college fair in 2013, tracked communications through 2018, application submitted in 2016
notable_or_distinctive: unusually concrete for this topic: the guest is an actual admissions administrator who screen-shares her institution's real CRM interface and walks through an actual applicant's tracked timeline
reliability_notes: guest explicitly notes the specific CRM/tracking setup shown is common but not universal, and practices vary by institution; otherwise a credible first-hand account with minimal garbling
